reviews.rationale: The module sequences one knowledge migration lifecycle; formatting, bootstrap application, terminal integration planning and apply, command error rendering, and top-level dispatch are extracted, while the remaining effects share ordered plan, approval, rollback, and event contracts.

Move, merge, split, and delete are variants of one exact-approved document-structure command contract and share the same validation, normalization-relocation reporting, materialization event, and rollback boundary.

All functions validate or execute one managed deliberation lifecycle and share the same provider plan, writing contract, checkpoint, and interruption semantics. Participant route validation, verified role composition, and organization-event mutation are isolated in the deliberation participant binding module; this module only orders binding, round execution, terminal release, and the existing lifecycle boundaries.

The module sequences one admitted run through context, execution, outcome checks, writing publication, finalization, and cleanup. Public command contracts, provider construction, grounded capability selection and package ceilings, and outcome verification are separate modules. Existing research, role, skill, workspace and project-verification owners retain their boundaries; the remaining lifecycle shares one ordered failure and storage-cleanup contract.

The module owns the immutable v1 base route catalog and composes additive protocol upgrades. Version-specific v4 through v11 additions remain in dedicated modules; command parsing, product inspection, projection policy, and rendering are separate. Its length is declarative catalog data rather than mixed execution responsibility.

TLS material loading, dependency and server composition, reload, resource lifecycle orchestration, and health wiring are phases of one Hub deployment boundary; HTTP connection-drain mechanics and domain policy remain in linked modules.

The class resolves one conversation event to a mode and dispatches its response through injected ports. Discussion eligibility, effect admission, intent conversion, and discussion response policy remain in dedicated modules; this boundary only selects the current event's available effects, caches its resolution, and routes the admitted result. ADR-0467 owner-turn capture is an injected port that only queues the turn.

The module composes one provider-neutral supervision runtime from storage, admission, reasoning, execution, and evidence ports. Request-origin evaluation, resource policy, provider effects, supersession, leases, snapshot projection, and wake scheduling with its observation gate remain in dedicated modules; this boundary only wires their ordered lifecycle and cleanup.

The class observes one bound goal for task, admission, owner-control, and cycle snapshots, and audits its history projection's tail for the wake schedule. It composes dedicated workforce, execution, authority, result, and handoff readers; effect execution, persistence, provider transport, domain policy, and runtime scheduling remain in separate modules. The two history projections share a canonical event chain but retain distinct task and authority scopes.

The class owns one external Claude protocol boundary and translates native session, tool, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; the accounting declaration remains in a linked descriptor module. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The class owns the Codex provider boundary, selects one injected native transport, and translates thread, turn, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; transport parsing and the accounting declaration remain linked modules. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The module executes one provider-neutral adapter conformance lifecycle from descriptor and session start through context, turn, telemetry, result identity, and stop; provider translation and focused binding rules remain in linked modules.

Read-only planning, per-role approval binding, and atomic agent or assignment transitions are phases of one workforce migration lifecycle; role resolution, capability resolution, state storage, event schemas, and CLI presentation remain behind linked package boundaries.

The module declaratively owns backward-compatible capability-report, route, and result-contract types from v1 through v11. Runtime composition, command parsing, product projection, persistence, and rendering remain in separate modules; its length follows the explicit versioned compatibility history rather than mixed implementation concerns.

The repository class owns one SQLite persistence boundary for platform bindings, including validation, reads, writes, and transaction-safe state changes. Inbound depth and the optional ordered active-target projection use only identities resolved at that same mapping boundary; participation, discussion scheduling, and turn ownership policy remain outside the adapter.

The module owns one in-memory deliberation state machine; publication failure recording, handoff materialization, snapshot restoration, event recording, and ADR-0460 usage verification decisions remain in linked modules. Methods enforce shared history and event invariants, record each artifact's verification state, and refuse convergence on an unverified artifact. Policy-role names stay provider-neutral metadata.

The module owns the event payload privacy boundary and its declarative registry. Context-quality field and semantic rules live in context-quality-payload.ts; adding that registry does not couple artifact storage, plan preparation, or writer activation into redaction.

The declarative migration catalog and migration runner own one versioned SQLite schema boundary; length is driven by schema history rather than mixed runtime policy. The ADR-0466 owner lease, ADR-0467 instruction candidate, ADR-0469 host continuity, and ADR-0477 delegation-bound definition tables are additive migrations.

One SQLite adapter composes repositories under the shared database, transaction, and schema lifecycle. Notification retention and waiting live in a separate adapter; this facade emits only committed scope coordinates and closes notifications with the store. Owner-lease, instruction-candidate, ADR-0469 host-record, and ADR-0477 definition methods only open a transaction around their own repositories.
Read, lint, query, export, import, and re-export are operations over one external OKF format boundary with shared safety, trust, and byte-preservation rules.

One provider-neutral run lifecycle delegates source capture, process observation, capability policy, result collection and verification to existing ports. Source admission uses the project-storage gate for the complete run; failed reference-result preservation stays behind its own CAS/evidence boundary. The coordinator sequences both without owning SQLite or background retry policy.

Reservation, completion, recovery projection, target binding, and integrity checks all operate on one immutable rollback replay table and transaction lifecycle; authorization and rollback policy remain outside the adapter.
The class owns one SQLite policy persistence boundary and its approval, verification, transaction, and query operations.

Declarative validation of one tracked layout contract: capacity, roles, routes with their prose descriptions, and legacy title terms read only for compatibility all report through the same JSON-pointer issue collector; loading, upgrade, and serialization live in the taxonomy module.

One isolated no-capability process boundary for both providers with native structured JSON output, shared availability translation, typed Codex failures, and the ADR-0479 reviewer-feedback instruction it adds only to envelopes carrying feedback. Admission, budgets, source policy and document effects stay outside. Common tests cover schema delivery, extraction, no tools, usage, cancellation and timeout.

The module sequences one owner publication (repair, scope check, replay, push, pull request, merge, supersession, local catch-up) into one durable state and failure code. ADR-0473 scope rules, repair planning and commits, Git mechanics, forge transport, body rendering, tip building, supersession ledgers, and state persistence are sibling modules; the remaining functions share one progress and failure contract.

Publication rendering, historical-document grouping, desired output construction, recorded-output comparison, and plan creation are phases of one deterministic structural compilation contract; historical marker detection lives in its own module.

Profiles, envelopes, candidate validation, lifecycle inspection, generation, candidate storage, planning, and exact-approved apply share one content-bound lifecycle. Observation, selection, worksets, shard cache, ADR-0473 tool ownership, and CLI rendering are separate; this module only threads tool-generated paths into eligibility and ADR-0479 reviewer feedback into envelopes, while feedback records and admission live in the convergence runtime.
Plan serialization, safe source inspection, merge planning, lineage updates, and apply are one atomic document-merge responsibility.

Destination safety, plan serialization, lineage, single-output normalization-record preservation, plan creation, and apply are one atomic document-move responsibility; normalization record mechanics remain in a separate bounded module and formatter configuration is outside this transaction.
Heading extraction, destination safety, plan serialization, lineage preservation, and apply are one atomic document-split responsibility.

One durable filesystem transaction owns staging, exact before/after bindings, publication, rollback and crash settlement. Apply snapshots operations, byte payloads and the document permit before acquiring its source gate; recovery captures the same root used for its gate. Terminal asset policy and validation remain in the runtime owner. Receipt interpretation stays with the caller; no provider or artifact policy enters the transaction.
Profile resolution, registry binding, structural refresh, plan creation, and exact-approved apply share one instruction-bridge lifecycle; target construction and classification are extracted.

Query behavior, safe publication access, and document drift findings were extracted; the remaining functions exclusively validate manifests, layout, normalization, lineage, and semantic sidecars and compose the extracted drift lint.
Coordinate extraction, candidate validation, protected-change review, plan creation, and apply implement one byte-safe README improvement contract.

Link rebasing, neutral ownership-record migration, machine moves, user updates, serialization, plan creation, and apply are phases of one repository-wide layout transaction. Source classification and its evidence observation live in the layout-candidate modules; taxonomy role-template refresh and tool-specific formatter configuration are outside this boundary.

Fresh filesystem discovery, safe reads, retries, lineage validation, supplemental evidence, and snapshot assembly own one scan. Pure classification, materialization, and transforms remain separate. Optional query-only source-unit reuse is supplied explicitly after fresh byte observation; the pure cache owns bindings and decoding, and a separate adapter owns persistence. Git-ignored path observation lives in git-ignored-paths.ts; the scan only skips what it reports.
Move, split, and merge lineage creation and validation operate on one lineage schema and safe registry-loading boundary.

One declarative package contract surface for scans, policy, lifecycle results, and typed failures. The optional ranker preparation projection is opaque and provider-neutral; validation belongs to the concrete adapter and persistence to query preparation. No implementation, filesystem, or concrete search adapter is imported into these contracts.

Current state, continuation import, start, update, and replicated import preserve one WorkstreamSnapshot aggregate, exact origin and predecessor invariants, CAS binding, intent-bound plan identity, and durable apply protocol. Snapshot construction, bookkeeping, revision derivation, freshness, and context rendering live in sibling modules, so this module keeps durable lifecycle orchestration only.

Identity calculation, registry validation, service-file inspection, onboarding planning, listing, and registration share one owner-only fleet registry contract; the exported service definition path is the same identity-to-path rule onboarding planning uses, so status readers cannot diverge from it.
The file is a declarative schema catalog for one adapter protocol; its length is data-shaped and contains no independent executable workflow.

The module contains only bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one organization-agent event catalog. Version-two deliberation participation fields extend the existing bound event additively; projection, privacy redaction, persistence, and execution remain in separate modules.

The module declares the unchanged schema-name mapping and forward-reference catalog used by build-time generation and public type names. It contains no compiler initialization, runtime validation, filesystem access, provider policy or artifact publication. Those responsibilities live in separate owners.

The module contains only the bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one terminal observation lifecycle; runtime validation, redaction, persistence, and orchestration remain in their owning modules.
Case validation, paired timing, quality aggregation, latency statistics, environment capture, and reporting form one reproducible benchmark protocol.

The module verifies one ordered, additive external-consumer protocol catalog from v1 through v11. It contains bounded expected descriptors only; repository journeys, product projection behavior, packaging, and release orchestration remain in separate scripts and focused tests.
Temporary project setup, process control, HTTPS calls, event observation, assertions, and cleanup compose one end-to-end acceptance scenario; command invocation is a separate thin entrypoint.

One coordinator owns exact predecessor validation, stable manager observations within the graceful stop bound, and transactional replacement for Hub, Node, host knowledge resident, and repository replica coordinator services; a same-definition restart needs a configuration transition. The renderer owns rendering and paths; transition selection, ADR-0489 recovery, and path-rewrite policy stay in adapters. Argument validation extraction remains the bounded roadmap follow-up.

The module composes the bounded suite, isolated workspaces, provider-neutral evidence selection, paired arm schedule, and cleanup; command invocation, versioned acceptance, report evaluation, provider preparation and transports, and selection policy remain separate.

The module owns one immutable comparison-contract lineage: protocols, schema, suite validation, and pure acceptance evaluation share the same version and gate lifecycle, while provider execution and evidence selection remain separate.

The module composes and validates one lineage of immutable provider-shadow contracts; policy, preparation I/O, execution, observation, and review remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit historical contract variants.
